description: The original home of the Saudi royal family and the first capital of the First Saudi State, built in distinctive Najdi mudbrick architectural style.
A clay and mudbrick fort in central Riyadh, famous as the site of King Abdulaziz's 1902 recapture of the city, an event that led to the founding of modern Saudi Arabia.
Saudi Arabia's first UNESCO World Heritage Site, featuring over 100 monumental Nabataean tombs carved into sandstone outcrops.
A towering sandstone rock formation naturally shaped like an elephant, one of AlUla's most recognizable natural landmarks.
Jeddah's historic old town, known for multi-story coral-stone tower houses with ornate wooden mashrabiya windows, and its role as a historic pilgrimage gateway.
A historic palace in Taif blending Ottoman, Indian, and local architectural styles, once used as a royal residence and now a cultural museum.
A striking stone-tower village in the Asir mountains, known for its multi-story fortified houses decorated with traditional Al-Qatt Al-Asiri art.
One of the oldest continuously inhabited oases in the region, tied to the ancient Dilmun civilization and Eastern Arabia's trading history.
